purpose: Proposed semantic decisions for governance report generation

decisions.statement: Queries execute in catalog order; results are collected into receipts before rendering any section of the report
Reconciliation must PASS before report is finalized; a report with RECONCILIATION_FAILED is not emitted
Every claim in the rendered report must have a valid pointer to a query result; missing pointers cause reconciliation failure
Running the report again on the same inputs must produce identical hashes and claim values; mismatches indicate data corruption
A receipt is stale if its scan ID does not match the current source index; stale receipts must be rerun

reportStructure.metadata-section: Report type, generated date, workspace, index ID, scan ID, query catalog, disposition
reportStructure.executive-summary: Summary statistics from feature-coverage and scenario-conformance queries
reportStructure.feature-drill-down: Per-feature analysis with scenarios, responsibilities, obligations
reportStructure.evidence-without-lineage: Inventory of unclassified mechanics and authority
reportStructure.reconciliation-section: Validation checks and claim pointer coverage
reportStructure.query-appendix: Full receipt artifacts with query, result, claim pointers

failureHandling.handlingStrategy: Stop execution; report which query failed and why; do not attempt partial recovery
Set reconciliation disposition to FAILED; include failure details in report; do not finalize
Increment missing-pointers count; flag in reconciliation; mark claim as unsupported
Fail reconciliation; report which value mismatched and hash mismatch

reconciliationChecks.assertion: Total registered claims equals sum of claims in all receipts
Every rendered claim has a valid pointer to a query result row
No query pointer is rendered twice for different claims
Result hash must match the deterministic serialization of the result
All receipts must reference the same scan ID as the current index
